paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson, and it's a heavy one: when the LORD tells you something clearly, no one else's word gets to overrule it. The man of God from Judah got his orders straight from the LORD: "You must not eat bread or drink water or return by the way you came." (1 Kings 13:9) He held that line against a king offering half of everything he owned, and then he dropped it for a plain invitation from an old prophet. I think this one hurts, because the old prophet was lying (1 Kings 13:18).

So what do we do with it? A voice can sound holy and still not line up with what God already said. The old prophet said, "I too am a prophet like you," and he said an angel spoke to him (1 Kings 13:18). Friend, I've been fooled by a shiny new stamper, so I know a smooth pitch can feel right, and that's why we test every voice against the Word we've already been given. And the cost was real. The word came that the man's body would never reach the tomb of his fathers, and the lion on the road showed that the LORD's word stands (1 Kings 13:22, 24).

Now look at the other side of the table. Jeroboam had a withered hand, a split altar and a prayer answered, and he still didn't repent (1 Kings 13:33). The LORD speaks, the LORD keeps His word, and what we do with it matters, whether we're a king or a prophet or a baker with a Bible. So learn the Word, hold on to it, and measure everything else by it. This kingdom's story isn't over yet, friend, so keep your apron on.
